doc.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Joining Benny Goodman through Juilliard, and meeting Mingus
summary: How a Juilliard dance teacher recommended him to Goodman, the nervous audition, the European tour and Goodman smoothing his exams; Mingus call followed.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Well after this change of career perhaps, you proceeded in a short number of years to play with a really wide variety of people, from Benny Goodman to Charles Mingus in the space of about a year?

As a matter of fact at the same time, during the same time. Benny Goodman came about as a result of, I think Teddy Wilson or somebody said no. He was supposed to do the Brussels Worlds Fair or do a tour in Europe. And somebody that he would normally call canceled and said no. And so he had the idea to call Juilliard and see if he could get some young person. And it just so happened that I was there at the time, and one of the teachers, the dance instructor, was a friend of Benny’s. She was a friend of Muriel Zuckerman. And I used to play dance classes, because I was always improvising. And she recommended me. So I went up to Benny Goodman’s house, and it’s a funny little story goes with this. He lived on 66th Street, just past Second Avenue. And I got to his apartment and I was just so nervous. The guy at the door says, “Can I help you?” I was so nervous I says, “Yes, I’d like to see Mr. Tommy Dorsey please.” And the guys said, “You mean Benny Goodman, don’t you?” I was just so nervous. But I never told Benny that.
That’s a good thing I think.

But anyway I went up and played for him. He asked me to play a couple of tunes and I played “Love for Sale,” and something else, something, I think “Yesterdays.” And he says okay, “You’ll be okay.” And then we had rehearsals. I met Arvell Shaw and Roy Burns and we went up to Stamford, Connecticut and rehearsed up there. And then I did the tour, I think I had to get permission from the school to take off and do the tour because although I wasn’t graduating, it would have some reflection on my grades. So I told Benny, I said, “Benny I’m not sure they’re going to let me do this.” So he called the school. “No problem, Mr. Goodman.” And he called from Europe after we were there, they extended the tour and he called from Europe and said, “He won’t be back for his exams, can you give him his exams in June?” Now school ended in May. And they said, “Mr. Goodman, no problem.” So he could do whatever he wanted to do. It didn’t matter. When I got back they gave me the exams, no problem. And soon after that, this was in 1958. Soon after that I had met Mingus before in 1957 up at some sort of camp, we were playing a summer festival and Mingus came up and sat in. And after I got back from Brussels, Mingus called me and asked me if I’d come and work some gigs with him. So it was the same year — ’58, ’59 — and I was still off and on with Benny until he hired me © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
